correctness.rationale: For all odd primes p, all dimensions d>=1 and all nondegenerate homogeneous quadratic Q, character orthogonality makes the base chirp CAZAC. Differentiate every nontrivial autocorrelation; a translated Fourier sum contributes e_p(-2Q(h))-1, giving the real Hessian multiplier 8N sin^2(2pi Q(h)/p). The B pairing is nonsingular, so Parseval identifies all eigenvalues and the zero-mode kernel. A standard diagonal Gauss sum exactly counts zeros by discriminant; fibers of B(s,.) establish exact isotropic-line torus deformations and span the Hessian nullspace. A positive-definite Hessian on mean-zero phases proves anisotropic local isolation by Taylor continuity, while torus deformations disprove isolation otherwise. Pure-Python standalone check succeeded: 140 quadratic zero-count cases, 10 independent finite-difference Hessian cases and 7 exact phase families. Floating tests are corroboration, not proof; no global classification is claimed.

evidence: Feichtinger–Kozek–Luef, arXiv:math/0703228 (first posted 2007-03-08), PDF introduction and §§3–4. Sections 3–4 give the finite-dimensional time-frequency operator framework, spreading representation and Gabor frame results; no result computes the real phase-autocorrelation Hessian at quadratic chirps.

Gilbert–Rzeszotnik, DOI:10.5802/aif.2556 (2010), printed MSC 42C40, PDF pp.1317–1320, 1341. The final section reports continuum families for cyclic orders divisible by squares; it does not classify quadratic forms on elementary abelian p-groups by split type.

Führ–Rzeszotnik, arXiv:1506.06738 (first posted 2015-06-19), PDF §§1 and 9, especially Theorem 9.18. Theorem 9.18 covers arbitrary unitary matrices and cyclic Fourier phasing manifolds abstractly, but it gives no scalar phase-Hessian spectrum or Gauss-count local dichotomy.
Classical bent-function split-form constructions may imply the existence of some exact isotropic line phase families; that known construction is not asserted original alone.

Banica, The defect of generalized Fourier matrices, arXiv:1210.2556 (first posted 2012-10-09), PDF introduction and Proposition 3.7/Theorem 5.6. Computes the full-matrix undephased tangent defect of group Fourier Hadamard matrices; Proposition 3.7 sets up circulant-case tangent equations but explicitly does not solve them. These are not the fixed-scalar quadratic chirp energy Hessian or its isotropic cone spectrum.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Theorems quantifying global existence, generic unitary phasing dimensions, and finite Gabor frame operators do not entail the full Hessian spectrum at each quadratic chirp. On elementary-abelian groups of the same order p^2, split and anisotropic quadratic forms have different nullities, so a cyclic-order-only criterion cannot dominate the new claim.

Direct equivalence: on a finite abelian group, zero off-origin autocorrelation is equivalent to unimodular normalized Fourier transform, by Fourier transformation of autocorrelation. The present theorem fixes the particular quadratic form and computes its full real phase Hessian.

A general complex-Hadamard defect formula specialized to these chirps remains a possible undiscovered equivalence.

originality.rationale: Closest inspected primary papers, including the Fourier-matrix defect literature, establish finite abelian Gabor harmonic analysis, general biunimodular Fourier extremizers and an abstract unitary phasing-manifold description. Their statements do not compute the full scalar phase-energy Hessian at nondegenerate odd-field quadratic forms, its all-rank Gauss-sum nullity, or the precise anisotropic local isolation versus isotropic torus dichotomy. Cyclic Gaussian-chirp rigidity on Z/NZ is not a statement about the noncyclic elementary-abelian groups F_p^d for d>=2. Known split-form bent families and one-dimensional chirp facts are explicitly excluded from standalone novelty claims. A residual equivalent-defect formulation is possible, but no decisive dominating source was found.
residual_risks: An older matrix-defect/circulant-Hadamard formula might specialize to the scalar chirp Hessian under a non-obvious reduction; Banica’s inspected full-matrix defect and unsolved circulant system are not direct coverage.

Classic Maiorana–McFarland and generalized bent-function constructions may already encompass each isolated isotropic-line deformation; only the combined rank, spectrum, and local criterion is assessed as new.
The source comparison is substantial but not an exhaustive worldwide bibliographic or independent review.

value.rationale: The result classifies exact local rigidity of a canonical family of perfect finite-field chirps, gives every phase-curvature eigenvalue and full degeneracy count for every rank and odd prime, and explains why products of one-dimensional locally rigid chirps can acquire arbitrarily many flat phase directions depending on arithmetic split type. The distinction between anisotropic rank-two chirps (one Hessian zero mode) and split rank-two chirps (2p−1 modes) is a structural obstruction relevant to stable constant-amplitude waveform design and finite Fourier geometry; it is more than a routine finite table evaluation. No paper-sized downstream theorem is asserted or required.
